newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt says no sign in Telstra vote.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt says no sign in Telstra vote.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Friday the government's victory in a Senate vote related to the sale of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp did not necessarily give hope that it would win legislative approval for the partial privatisation of Telstra.
The two key independent senators backed the government in Friday's vote, but Alston said: "I don't think it tells you anything about their attitude to the ultimate outcome."

Non-government parties in the Senate had sought to split the bill into two parts separately authorising the sale and imposing minimum service requirements that the government has offered as a sweetener to get the bill through.
But Independents Brian Harradine and Mal Colston sided with the government and defeated the move.
Colston and Harradine are crucial to the passage of the Telstra legislation as the government needs two extra votes to pass any legislation in the Senate.
The non-government parties are opposed to the sale.
The government plans to raise A$8 billion from the one-third sale of Telstra with A$1 billion of that earmarked for its environmental upgrade programme.
